subject: Private deployment connectivity options for Acme Analytics — decision and pilot request
messages:
From: Luis Ramos <luis.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Infra Team <infra-team@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity options for our inference gateway

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Acme Analytics is moving toward a Private deployment with Redwood (we'll host the gateway in our AWS account but keep model hosting in Redwood Dedicated). A few constraints I want to call out up front:

- On-prem datacenter has a stateful firewall and strict NAT rules; the security team wants explicit per-service access controls.
- We need auditability (who called what, when) for HIPAA compliance.
- We'd prefer a single, supported connection path for production; a VPN PoC is fine for a trial.
- We have a transit VPC pattern today for other SaaS connections and are open to re-using it if necessary.

Can you advise trade-offs between: VPC peering (cross-account), PrivateLink / interface endpoints, and a site-to-site VPN (IPsec)? Which would you recommend for: low latency, auditability, and easiest path to an SLA-backed production rollout?

I've attached a simple network diagram and the current on-prem WAN egress plan. Happy to hop on a call if that helps. Procurement needs a recommendation by end of next week.

--
Luis Ramos
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Analytics
(luis.ramos@acme-analytics.com)

Attachment: acme-network-diagram.pdf (diagram, 1 page)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ramos <luis.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options for our inference gateway

Luis — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. High level first, then a recommended path for pilot + production: 

Quick trade-offs (short):
- VPC peering: cheapest for data transfer and lowest added latency when both VPCs are within the same region and there is no IP overlap. Downsides: cross-account peering can get messy at scale (many peering relationships), no per-service access control, and no private endpoint auditing out of the box.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): best for per-service access control, strong isolation (no route table changes between accounts), and easy to tie into AWS endpoint policies and KMS-based auditing. Costs are per ENI + data processing. Works well if you can front the Redwood gateway with an NLB that accepts PrivateLink.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec): quickest to stand up for a PoC, provides encrypted transport, and can traverse existing transit setups. Downsides: harder to scale (throughput & MTU), often higher latency, and you'd need to wire in flow logs/audit separately.

My recommended path for Acme: run a two-week PrivateLink pilot (secure, auditable, and maps cleanly to your policy wants). For the pilot we can allow a fallback S2S VPN for non-critical traffic while endpoint limits and cost profiling are validated. If you absolutely need the lowest possible latency intra-VPC for heavy inter-service token exchange we can consider peering later, but PrivateLink gives more control and aligns with audit needs.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Karthik and I will produce a short connectivity matrix (ENI counts, estimated monthly cost, IP overlap risk, monitoring hooks).
2) Set up a 60-minute architecture call (Wed or Thu this week) to review.
3) Pilot SOW + mutual action plan to scope the PrivateLink proof-of-value (2 weeks).

Attaching a starter connectivity matrix (lightweight) to help procurement. If that looks OK I'll ask legal to prepare a short pilot SOW and send a DocuSign link.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-connectivity-matrix.xlsx (sheet: pilot-estimates)

Luis / Jasmine — adding a few technical points to help procurement and security weigh options: 

- IP addressing: If Acme's on-prem ranges overlap with our recommended gateway ranges, VPC peering will force a renumber or NAT; PrivateLink avoids that because traffic terminates at an ENI in Acme's VPC.
- Auditing & tracing: PrivateLink + NLB path allows us to attach VPC flow logs, ALB/NLB access logs, and Redwood runtime tracing to the same per-connection endpoint. Peering has no endpoint abstractions; you'd need flow logs at the VPC/subnet level which is noisier.
- Performance: For small bursty request patterns (typical for inference control-plane calls and short prompt traffic) the performance delta between PrivateLink and peering is negligible. If you plan large streaming inference payloads (multi-MB per request), peering can be cheaper due to data processing charges on endpoints.
- VPN specifics: Common pain points we've seen — MTU fragmentation (path MTU discovery issues), rekeying causing transient drops, and throughput limits on customer firewalls. Also make sure IPSec lifetimes are tuned for long-running streaming connections if you plan to use them for model inference payloads.
- Cross-region: If Acme needs multi-region redundancy, PrivateLink will require endpoints in each region; peering doesn't help cross-region since peering is region-specific. S2S VPN can cross-connect but will add latency.

I've added estimated ENI counts and data charges to the matrix Jasmine attached. For auditing we can also enable log forwarding to your SIEM via our native log push (we sign an agreement for log retention and delivery in the pilot SOW).

Link to our internal networking handbook (public to your team for context): https://redwood.app/handbook/private/networking

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Jasmine & Karthik — this is helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups from security/procurement: 

1) Auditing: you mentioned pushing logs to our SIEM. Can you confirm retention windows and format (CloudWatch logs -> Kinesis -> SIEM vs S3 delivery)? We need field-level timestamps and caller identity mapped to our SSO IDs.
2) Costs: procurement wants a ballpark monthly estimate for a single-region pilot (approx 50k requests / month, average payload ~120KB). Your matrix had a small line item but can you confirm the P-List vs peering delta?
3) Endpoint quotas: we have some internal experience with AWS ENI quotas being hit during large program rollouts. Will you help coordinate quota increases if needed?

Procurement deadline: end of next week. We're leaning toward PrivateLink if the numbers and quotas work. If you can send a short mutual action plan and a pilot SOW we can sign, that would speed things up.

--
Luis

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options for our inference gateway — pilot MAP + SOW

Luis — thanks for the questions. Short answers + next actions below so procurement can move forward: 

Auditing & logs: we can deliver structured logs to your SIEM in two supported ways: (1) CloudWatch Logs -> Kinesis Firehose -> your SIEM (near-real-time, JSON records including timestamp, request id, internal caller id) or (2) batched S3 delivery (for archival) with the same JSON schema. Default retention for the pilot will be 90 days; we can extend per contract. I'll include the log schema in the SOW.

Costs: rough pilot estimate (single us-east-1 region, 50k req/month, payload 120KB): 
- PrivateLink (ENI + data processing): ~$1,200/mo (endpoints + data)
- VPC Peering (data transfer): ~$800/mo
- VPN (managed + egress): ~$600/mo but with higher ops overhead and potential throughput costs on your firewall.
Exact numbers in the attached CSV — these are conservative estimates.

ENI quotas: yes — Redwood will coordinate with Acme to request necessary ENI limits and monitor usage during the pilot. We do this regularly as part of our onboarding checklist.

Attached: a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and the pilot SOW (DocuSign link included). If you approve, Ben will coordinate the legal/purchase order and I will kick off the technical onboarding with Karthik.

Proposed MAP highlights: 
- Pilot window: 2 weeks (private-link endpoint in us-east-1)
- Success criteria: <200ms p99 for control-plane calls, logs present in SIEM within 30s, no ENI quota throttling
- Owner: Acme infra + Redwood SE (Karthik)
- Sign-off: Procurement approval + security review

DocuSign (pilot SOW): https://app.docusign.com/ACME-PRIVATE-PLINK-SOW-12345

If this looks OK I'll have Ben open the PO thread and Legal will attach the SOW.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
